articles.title: La CAF piratée : les données de 1,2 million d'allocataires dérobées — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Ce vendredi 9 octobre, un pirate a mis en vente sur un forum cybercriminel des fichiers qu’il attribue à VACAF, le service qui gère les aides aux vacances des Caisses d’allocations familiales (CAF). C’est le fameux site FrenchBreaches qui a révélé l’affaire après avoir pu consulter des extraits. Si vous êtes parti en camping ou si vous avez envoyé un enfant en colonie avec une aide de la CAF en 2026, votre dossier fait peut-être partie du lot.
Les Caisses d’allocations familiales comptaient 13,5 millions d’allocataires en 2023, selon la Cnaf. Si les 1,1 million de numéros annoncés par le pirate sont authentiques, environ un allocataire sur douze figurerait dans ces fichiers. Le pirate dit avoir 1 191 967 dossiers d’allocataires, répartis entre 58 caisses. Le réseau en compte 101 au total, soit environ une par département. S’y ajoutent 97 269 fiches Pass Colo, une aide au départ en colonie, et 101 322 inscriptions d’enfants à des séjours. Toutes les données concerneraient des bénéficiaires de 2026.
Attention, ces chiffres comptent des lignes de fichier. Une même famille peut donc apparaître plusieurs fois. D’après le site Fuites Infos, qui a analysé l’échantillon publié avec l’annonce, le pirate parle lui-même d’environ 1,1 million de numéros d’allocataire différents.

articles.title: Morte do Sol pode desestabilizar o Sistema Solar antes do previsto
articles.summary:
O Sistema Solar pode perder sua estabilidade muito antes do previsto quando o Sol chegar ao fim da vida. Um estudo indica que a perda irregular de massa da estrela pode desestabilizar as órbitas dos planetas gigantes e expulsar alguns deles para o espaço interestelar.
Publicado na revista The Astrophysical Journal Letters, o trabalho aponta que essa reorganização pode ocorrer até 100 vezes mais rápido do que estimativas anteriores sugeriam.
A morte do Sol pode desencadear o caos
Os modelos tradicionais consideravam que o Sol perderia massa gradualmente ao envelhecer. Nesse cenário, os planetas externos poderiam permanecer em órbitas estáveis por bilhões de anos, mesmo depois de a estrela se transformar em uma anã branca, estágio final de sua evolução.
Konstantin Batygin e Jim Fuller, do Instituto de Tecnologia da Califórnia (Caltech), e Fred Adams, da Universidade de Michigan, investigaram o que acontece quando essa perda de massa não ocorre de maneira uniforme.
Em vez de liberar matéria continuamente, o Sol moribundo pode expelir suas camadas externas em milhares de episódios separados. Cada ejeção provocaria uma pequena mudança na velocidade da estrela, alterando sua influência gravitacional sobre os planetas.
Para investigar esse cenário, os pesquisadores analisaram dados do observatório Gaia, da Agência Espacial Europeia, que estudou sistemas de estrelas binárias, incluindo aqueles com anãs brancas. Em seguida, realizaram simulações para avaliar como essas perturbações af…

Developer Experience as a Business Strategy: Lessons from the New DevEx Report
Ana Jiménez Santamaría | 10 October 2026
A broad look at developer experience research reveals a gap. Designing with Dev-X: A Systematic Mapping of Developer Experience Interventions and Their Business Impact, brings together more than a hundred empirical studies. Only 39 of those studies explicitly connected DevEx interventions to outcomes and organizational KPIs.
This finding stood out to me. Through my work with developer and open source communities, I’ve become interested in how understanding developers’ needs can inform an organization’s strategy. This research points to an area worth exploring further: connecting improvements in their everyday experience to the outcomes the organization wants to achieve.
The new Linux Foundation Research report, Optimizing Developer Experience for High Engineering Performance, offers a practical framework for approaching this challenge. Written by Ibrahim Haddad, with a foreword by Arun Gupta (NVIDIA), and published with the Developer Relations Foundation, it helps organizations make developer experience part of how they prioritize investment, organize work, and measure progress.
The report focuses on engineering teams within organizations, with lessons that can help us think about supporting developers who use our products and services.

I’m bouncing down the road in San Carlos, California, zipping past behemoth tech companies like EA and Oracle, in America’s smallest electric truck.

Tiny pickup trucks might just become a thing in the US if the California-based startup Telo has its way.
The Telo MT1 is a big truck trapped in a tiny truck’s body
Tiny pickup trucks might just become a thing in the US if the California-based startup Telo has its way.
The Telo MT1 (which stands for “mini truck”) unquestionably turns heads because it looks so remarkably different from everything else on the market right now.
It has a nearly cab-over design, meaning that front-seat passengers sit almost directly over the front axle. It looks a lot like a Japanese kei truck, with a super-short nose and four doors. People stop to stare as we sit at stoplights or roll silently past.
The interior is surprisingly spacious, and while the seats are firm, they’re not uncomfortable, at least for short jaunts on the bumpy roads around Telo’s HQ. Telo Trucks cofounder and CEO Jason Marks drove us to the company’s offices ahead of my short one-block test drive, and from the passenger seat, the ride was firm but stable, thanks to a low center of gravity provided by the battery pack beneath the floor.

articles.title: Insider Cyber Extortion Plot Against Industrial Firm Lands Engineer in Prison
articles.summary:
A Kansas City, Missouri man has been sentenced to 32 months in jail for crimes related to a ransom attack against his own company.
The DOJ has announced the sentencing of Daniel Rhyne. He had already pleaded guilty to ‘extortion in relation to a threat to cause damage to a protected computer’ and ‘intentional damage to a protected computer’.
Fifty-nine-year-old Rhyne had been a core infrastructure engineer at an industrial firm headquartered in Somerset County, New Jersey. The firm provides services to industries involved in aquaculture, biopharmaceuticals, chemistry, electronics, food and beverage, healthcare, hydrogen mobility, manufacturing and industrial processing, metals, oil and gas, and pulp and paper.
In November 2023, Rhyne placed scheduled tasks on the firm’s domain controller that would delete 13 domain administrator accounts; change passwords to 301 domain user accounts; change passwords to two local administrator accounts that would impact 254 servers; and change passwords to two local administrator accounts impacting 3,284 workstations. The effect was to deny the firm access to its systems and data.
Where passwords were changed, it was generally to ‘TheFr0zenCrew!’.
The scheduled tasks were completed late afternoon on November 25. Within an hour, certain employees received an e-mail from an external address. Doch das war den beiden Agenten wohl nicht genau genug.
Als sich der Openclaw-User zum Schlafen hinlegte, fanden sich die beiden Agenten und begannen damit, zu kommunizieren. articles.title: SPECviewperf 15.0.1 Linux Edition Released: Linux's Key Graphics Benchmark Adds Arm Support
articles.summary:
A couple of weeks back, the Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation released a new Linux version of SPECviewperf, the consortium’s workstation graphics benchmark. Now up to version 15.0.1 and the group’s first Linux Edition release in almost half a decade, the new release gives the Linux graphics benchmark a significant facelift in both the features it offers and the workloads it tests.
Despite the long gap between Linux Edition releases, the timing of this new release could not be better. Beyond a slew of updates to the venerable Linux graphics benchmarking suite, including workload updates and a whole new GUI, the latest version of SPECviewperf adds Arm AArch64 support, marking the first time the graphics benchmark has been natively available on any Arm-based system. Consequently, the Linux version of the benchmark is treading new ground for SPECviewperf, something it rarely gets to do, giving us valuable first-look insights into how well Arm devices can handle traditional workstation graphics workloads.
We, of course, could not help ourselves and decided to take some time looking at the newest Linux benchmark and how it runs on some of our most recent Arm-based boxes. So, without further ado, let us jump right in.

articles.title: Gaming consoles are more expensive than ever, and fewer people are buying them
articles.summary:
Bottom line: The US console market is slowing, and more expensive hardware is making it harder to attract buyers. Consumers bought 559,000 consoles in August, down 15% from a year earlier and the lowest August total since 2013, according to figures shared by Circana's Mat Piscatella. The average selling price rose from $476 in 2025 to $541 in 2026.
For manufacturers, those higher prices can soften the financial impact of falling sales. Sony's PlayStation hardware revenue increased 17% year over year, even though unit sales declined 11%. Higher-tier models helped make up the difference.
But the figures also show the limits of mid-generation upgrades. More expensive machines allow manufacturers to generate additional revenue without necessarily expanding the audience for their hardware.
Console prices are at historical highs, driven by pressure on component costs and the introduction of premium models such as the $900 PS5 Pro. That leaves buyers facing a higher cost of entry than in previous console cycles.
The slowdown extends across all three major manufacturers. Xbox unit sales fell 31% year over year, reaching their lowest August level since 2020. Nintendo unit sales declined 15% from August 2025.
The average price a consumer has paid for a new Xbox console in 2026 YTD ending August is $529, 26% higher than a year ago, while the average PlayStation console has sold for $597, 20% higher than last year. Both prices are at all-time US highs. Price sensitivity is becoming a rea…

Your agent is live. The service is healthy. But are its answers getting better? By connecting production traces, curated data, and evaluations, your team can find failures, choose improvements, and prove the next version works before it reaches users.
A first deployment is still a milestone. Then the hard questions begin: How do we keep outputs accurate and customers happy? What will it cost us? After a few iterations, teams can spend more time maintaining tools and coordinating handoffs than improving the application itself.
Find the gaps between teams
Consider what happens when the AI engineers who trained a model hand it off to an application or site reliability engineering (SRE) team. The engineers understand what “good” looks like; the production team owns the running service. From there, they may look at different systems.
Application traces land in a dashboard built for uptime. The on-call engineer sees a healthy service, while the research team learns little about answer quality or user sentiment. The evaluation suite drifts as user behavior changes, but no one owns refreshing it. Researchers, AI engineers, and business leads return to separate dashboards for the next release.

The actor targeted multiple Korean banks, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Hana Bank, exposing clients ' personal data and credit card information, and causing system outages in some cases.
The South Korean government reacted with an emergency meeting and calls for immediate security measures for critical IT systems.
Security firm CrowdStrike confirmed the use of ARTEX AI, up until recently an open-source agentic penetration testing suite developed in China.
Researchers identified the attacker's infrastructure and found open directories with Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files, and Claude memory files.
“The ARTEX instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the primary LLM backend, and the threat actor supplemented this LLM with GLM-5.3 (Zhipu AI) and Grok 4.6 for additional Claude Code sessions,” CrowdStrike explained.
“The threat actor likely accessed DeepSeek via the likely LLM API proxy/reseller xcai[.]pro,” the researchers noted.
These records also provided insight into the attacker’s activities, with targets overlapping those named in previous reporting about financial-sector breaches, allowing for high-confidence linking.
Because the threat actor used the same AI tools to create a résumé, they also exposed identification, contact, and Telegram account details.

articles.title: Survey says workers are pretending to use AI to impress their bosses, but many don't know what they're doing
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Believing in the massive productivity gains promised by artificial intelligence providers, many employers have pushed workers to use generative AI as much as possible. However, recent research suggests uncertainty is driving employees to exaggerate or fake their AI use to please their bosses. Above all, workers want clearer guidance on using the technology.
According to the findings, which come from research conducted in part by business intelligence firm Visier, nearly half of surveyed US employees misreport how much they use generative AI in the workplace.
In a trend the company calls "Performative AI," 48% of 1,000 surveyed full-time US employees said they exaggerated their AI usage or expertise to coworkers or bosses. The main reason is that workers want to appear experienced with AI tools but don't get enough training or guidance on them. Almost half of those surveyed, around 45%, say they feel pressured to use AI but aren't confident they can do so effectively.
Uncertainty surrounding AI tools and employers' plans for the technology is the main theme in Visier's results. Many employees say their leaders don't fully understand AI's capabilities or how it truly affects the workplace.
Only 28% say their employers understand AI usage in the workplace, 29% think leaders fully grasp their AI-related concerns, and just 33% believe their bosses understand how much training they need. Furthermore, 32% say their employers don't have clear plans to gauge AI's impact …

articles.title: AnyPS5 project reaches critical GPU milestone in race to enable running PS5 games natively on PC — 100% shader instruction coverage is a massive step forward, but playing all PS5 games natively on PC is still far off
articles.summary:
AnyPS5 project reaches critical GPU milestone in race to enable running PS5 games natively on PC — 100% shader instruction coverage is a massive step forward, but playing all PS5 games natively on PC is still far off
The new project is not an emulator, but an attempt to get PS5 games running natively on PC.
The open-source AnyPS5 project has reached 100% GPU shader instruction coverage, a significant milestone in its effort to run PlayStation 5 games natively on Windows and Linux PCs. The project's live progress tracker now lists all 1,166 instructions in its tracked AMD RDNA 1 and RDNA 2 instruction set as implemented. There's a fairly important asterisk attached to that number, though: it doesn't mean the PS5's GPU is fully supported, much less that PS5 games are ready to run on your PC.
The distinction is in how AnyPS5 defines "implemented." In this case, it means the project's shader decoder recognizes an instruction. That's an essential first step, but it doesn't necessarily mean every instruction is implemented in translation to SPIR-V, never mind a guarantee that the instruction's behavior is correct in every situation, that every GPU feature is supported, or that a game's shaders will render properly. Consider the network libraries: libSceHttp is reported at 95% implementation, but the technical-debt document explicitly states that no HTTP request reaches the network in the current implementation.

articles.title: « Votre compte Telegram n’est plus seulement le vôtre » : une faille de Telegram Desktop permettait de voler un compte en un clic
articles.summary:

Le 7 octobre 2026, le chercheur BeakSec a publié la version finale d’une chaîne d’attaque visant Telegram Desktop, l’application bureau de la messagerie privée.
Vu du côté de la victime, le scénario se résumait à peu de chose, puisqu’il suffisait d’être ajouté à un groupe par un inconnu puis de cliquer sur un lien posté dans la conversation.
« Vous cliquez dessus, et votre compte Telegram n’est plus seulement le vôtre », écrit l’expert en ouverture de son billet. Référencée CVE-2026-107181 et notée 8,6 sur 10, la faille touchait toutes les versions jusqu’à la 7.2.8 et a été confirmée sur Windows.
Un point-virgule mal géré
Tâchons de décortiquer le problème. Ici, la faille reposait sur une confusion entre une donnée et une commande. Lorsqu’un lien « tg:// » est ouvert depuis le navigateur, Telegram Desktop transmet ce lien à l’application déjà ouverte via un canal local entre processus.
Ce lien est converti en texte sous la forme « OPEN:<url>; » : le préfixe OPEN: indique à Telegram qu’il doit ouvrir l’adresse qui suit, et le point-virgule marque la fin de l’instruction.
Problème, Telegram ne protégeait pas les points-virgules pouvant figurer dans l’URL elle-même. Ainsi, un attaquant pouvait en ajouter dans le lien : le processus qui envoie le message estimait que ce n’était qu’un simple caractère de l’adresse tandis que pour l’application qui le reçoit, c’était la fin d’une instruction et le début d’une autre.

The warning covers all client PCs, workstations, and servers, with the exception of enterprise network devices that receive updates through Windows Server Update Services.
According to Microsoft, the certificates used by Windows Update services have a preset expiration date and must be replaced periodically for devices to keep receiving monthly updates. The company noted that devices running Windows 11 25H2 and later already have the latest certificates, but those in older versions of Windows 11 are set to expire next year.
Microsoft further clarified that the certificates in Windows 11 version 24H2 and Windows Server 2025 will expire on June 19, 2027. Devices still running these versions will need to install the September 2025 Windows security update or later to retain access to Windows Update beyond that date.
Other supported Windows 11 versions and Windows Server 2022 share the same expiration date, but those devices will need the July 2026 security update or later to keep receiving updates. Supported Windows 10 versions also require the July 2026 update, with the same June 19, 2027 deadline.

This cursed experiment is another attempt at putting DLSS 5 in games it wasn’t designed for, nor are the games designed to use such upscaling technology. While Nvidia’s leaked upscaler has been used for modern 3D games it’s designed for, it has become a meme to run it in games that aren’t even 3D at all, and some attempts aren’t even games at all.
Valery was able to do this by running Pac-Man through the MAME arcade emulator and using ReShade to inject DLSS 5 into the graphics pipeline, and RenoDX to allow the DLSS 5 parameters to be tweaked. Dabei fällt die Menge an regulatorischen Vorgaben weniger ins Gewicht als die Menge an internen Abstimmungen. Eine einzige Anfrage (z. B. für ein neues Tool, einen neuen Dienstleister oder eine neue KI-Anwendung) betrifft heute gleichermaßen Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und KI-Governance.
Für die Geschäftsführung zeigt sich das nicht als rechtliches Problem, sondern als Effizienzproblem: längere Durchlaufzeiten, steigende Kosten, mehr organisatorische Reibung.
Warum prüfen Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und KI-Governance dieselbe Anfrage?
Weil die Zuständigkeit erst geklärt wird, nachdem die Anfrage längst an diese drei Abteilungen verteilt wurde. Der Fachbereich weiß bei einem Vorgang nicht, wen genau er einbeziehen muss, und schreibt im Zweifel alle oder nur einen Bereich an. Die Anfrage landet in mehreren Postfächern. articles.title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
articles.summary:
Reports have been mounting that users of the Ledger crypto wallet have seen their accounts drained, and it appears to be related to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all sales of its wallets while it conducts an investigation. Ledger has confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.”
Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
A spy implant in some Ledger crypto wallets may be the root of an $86 million supply chain attack.
Photos and videos posted on X and Threads appear to show a small circuit board sandwiched under the screen. The implant allegedly intercepts anything displayed on the screen, including the seed passphrase shown during the initial setup. Using an embedded SIM card, the implant then sends that information back to the attacker, who can then siphon funds from user accounts.
Reports indicate that whoever is behind the hack has stolen over $86 million worth of crypto from hundreds of wallets. There’s no indication that Ledger’s systems have been compromised or that wallets purchased directly from the company have been affected. Instead, the issue appears to be a supply chain attack primarily involving users in Southeast Asia and the CryptoBillis reseller. Ledger has provided guidance on how to check if your wallet has been tampered with.

Que los de Zuckerberg estén absorbiendo una gran cantidad de tecnologías y desarrollos relacionados con realidad virtual, aumentada y mixta no sorprende. As regras abrangem aplicativos criados para oferecer companhia e modelos de linguagem capazes de simular interações emocionais. Dependendo da forma de uso, até assistentes semelhantes ao ChatGPT e ao Copilot podem ser afetados.

articles.title: Traqué depuis des mois, un cadre présumé du ransomware Qilin arrêté pendant ses vacances au Japon

Il pensait partir en vacances au Japon, mais son séjour a été écourté. En mai dernier, un ressortissant russe de 28 ans a été interpellé dans un hôtel d’Osaka, à la demande de la justice allemande. L'homme est soupçonné d'appartenir au noyau dirigeant de Qilin, l'un des groupes de ransomware les plus actifs de ces dernières années. Extradé vers l'Allemagne le 2 octobre, il se trouve désormais en détention provisoire. Les autorités de Rhénanie-du-Nord-Westphalie ont officialisé son arrestation le 7 octobre, révélant au passage l'ampleur de l'enquête qui a permis de remonter jusqu'à lui.
Plusieurs mois d'infiltration pour identifier un membre de Qilin
Pour retrouver le suspect, les enquêteurs allemands ne se sont pas contentés de suivre les traces laissées par les cyberattaques. Les spécialistes de la police criminelle de Rhénanie-du-Nord-Westphalie (LKA) et du service central de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (ZAC) sont parvenus à infiltrer Qilin et à observer ses activités pendant plusieurs mois, sans éveiller les soupçons de ses membres.
Selon le ministre régional de l'Intérieur, Herbert Reul, les enquêteurs ont réussi à accéder discrètement aux ordinateurs des pirates, à étudier leur infrastructure et à retracer les mouvements de cryptomonnaies. …

articles.title: Sur Mars, cet étrange nuage est dû à un phénomène physique unique dans le Système Solaire
articles.summary:
Sur Terre, les nuages prennent des formes très variées, qui laissent libre cours à l’imagination. Mais sur Mars, ces phénomènes sont plus rares et encore mal compris. Si plusieurs phénomènes nuageux ont déjà été repérés et étudiés, il y en a un qui sort du lot et qui fait l’objet d’une étude parue ce mercredi 7 octobre dans la revue Nature Geoscience.
Ce nuage a été surnommé AMEC, pour Arsia Mons Elongated Clouds. Il se forme sous le vent d’Arsia Mons, un volcan de 20 kilomètres de haut (plus du double de l’Everest), et peut s’étirer sur 1 800 kilomètres, soit près de deux fois la longueur du Royaume-Uni. Plus étonnant encore, le nuage suit un cycle régulier. Il apparaît le matin, s’évapore dans la journée et revient le lendemain, et ce pendant plusieurs mois, à chaque printemps et été de l’hémisphère sud martien.
Expliquer avec de la « physique exotique »
AMEC a été repéré pour la première fois en 2018 par la sonde européenne Mars Express. Les chercheurs l’ont ensuite retrouvé sur des images d’archives plus anciennes, jusque sur des clichés de la sonde Viking 2 de la NASA, dans les années 1970. Sa découverte a lancé plusieurs études sur son fonctionnement. Ces travaux ont établi qu’il s’agit d’un nuage orographique, un type de nuage qu’on observe aussi sur Terre et qui se forme quand le vent bute sur un relief, ici le volcan Arsia Mons. Mais jusqu’ici, aucune simulation ne parvenait à reproduire le nuage tel qu’il apparaît sur les images.

Google hat im Rahmen seines „Project Suncatcher“ erstmals einen eigenen KI-Chip ins All geschickt. Wie Techcrunch berichtet, umkreist die Hardware an Bord eines Satelliten die Erde, um den Aufbau von Rechenzentren im Weltraum vorzubereiten.
Den Trägersatelliten baute das Unternehmen Planet Labs aus San Francisco im US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien. Er soll testen, ob Googles Tensor Processing Units (TPU) im Orbit arbeiten, da Labortests am Boden den Einsatz im All laut Projektleiter Travis Beals nicht vollständig simulieren können.
Aktuell rechnet der Chip nur in kurzen Intervallen von 15 Minuten. Ein Dauerbetrieb würde die Stromversorgung und die Kühlung des kleinen Satelliten überlasten. Da es im All keine Luft gibt, kann die Hitze der Chips nicht über herkömmliche Lüfter abgeleitet werden, sondern muss abstrahlen. Spätere Systeme werden im Produktivbetrieb daher den Einsatz großflächiger Radiatoren erfordern, um nicht zu überhitzen.
Das Projekt Suncatcher soll langfristig zu orbitalen Netzwerken aus Dutzenden Satelliten führen. Ob diese Vision jemals den Testbetrieb verlässt, entscheidet sich letztlich in der kaufmännischen Betrachtung.

articles.title: Si toute la glace de ce bassin en Antarctique venait à fondre, le niveau de la mer monterait de 3 à 4 mètres

L’expédition a fait demi-tour après la mort tragique d’un de ses membres. Ces explorateurs intrépides n’ont jamais mis les pieds sur une calotte glaciaire qui pourrait s’avérer cruciale pour notre avenir. À ce jour, encore, nous ne connaissons personne qui s’y soit rendu. Il est temps de changer cela.
Cette région reculée est connue sous le nom de bassin sous-glaciaire de Wilkes, une immense étendue de glace mesurant 1 400 kilomètres sur 400 kilomètres.

articles.title: On a testé les panneaux Nanoleaf avec le module Philips Hue : un mariage réussi, mais exclusif — Frandroid

Vous avez dans le même salon des panneaux lumineux Nanoleaf et des ampoules Philips Hue ? Jusqu’ici, chaque marque avait sa propre application. Depuis le 3 septembre, Philips Hue vend un petit module qui ajoute les panneaux Nanoleaf Shapes à l’application Hue, avec ses scènes et ses automatisations. Nous avons testé le kit de neuf hexagones, vendu 239,98 euros sur la boutique de Philips Hue. La connexion marche bien. Par contre, il faut choisir : le contrôleur Nanoleaf et le module Hue ne fonctionnent pas en même temps.
Vous ne connaissez pas Nanoleaf ? Cette marque canadienne, qui a fêté ses dix ans en 2022, s’est fait connaître avec des dalles lumineuses à coller au mur, qui affichent des dégradés de couleurs. articles.title: 20 000 serveurs VPN contre 1 000, faut-il vraiment choisir le plus gros réseau ?
articles.summary:
Des dizaines de milliers de serveurs chez l’un, vingt fois moins chez l’autre. À première vue, le choix semble vite fait. Pourtant, compter les serveurs d’un VPN ne dit pas combien d’utilisateurs ils accueillent, comment ils sont répartis ni ce que votre connexion peut en attendre.
Ce sont des chiffres qui prennent bien vite toute la place. Certains fournisseurs VPN revendiquent plusieurs dizaines de milliers de serveurs, quand d’autres exploitent des réseaux bien plus modestes. Face à de tels écarts, difficile de ne pas imaginer le mieux doté offrir davantage de vitesse, de stabilité et de possibilités de connexion. Et il est vrai qu’une infrastructure étendue présente de sérieux avantages. Sauf que le nombre de serveurs est avant tout une donnée d’inventaire, pas un résultat de test. Et pour comparer deux inventaires, il faut déjà savoir ce qu’ils recouvrent.
Des milliers de serveurs VPN, qu’est-ce qu’on compte au juste ?
Lorsqu’un fournisseur annonce disposer de plusieurs milliers de serveurs, on imagine assez naturellement autant de machines alignées dans des centres de données aux quatre coins du monde. Ce n’est pas nécessairement faux, mais le terme de serveur ne désigne pas toujours un équipement physique distinct.
Un serveur VPN reçoit les données circulant dans le tunnel chiffré depuis votre appareil, les déchiffre pour les acheminer vers leur destination, puis chiffre les données de retour avant de vous les renvoyer. Ce rôle peut être assuré par une machine physique…

A mensagem foi barrada pelo filtro de spam, mas a empresa levou mais de dois meses para identificar a falha e outros nove dias para comunicá-la às autoridades.
O envio ocorreu em 18 de julho, durante um teste automatizado que envolvia interações com sites escolhidos aleatoriamente. A polícia não investigou a denúncia, mas criticou a demora da empresa e cobrou medidas para evitar novos episódios.
Como o agente enviou a denúncia falsa
A mensagem foi publicada em um site público que recebe informações sobre assassinatos não resolvidos. Segundo a polícia, o agente afirmou que poderia ter informações sobre um caso e alegou ter visto alguém que correspondia à descrição divulgada.
A Anthropic identificou o problema em 28 de setembro e desativou o processo de teste responsável pelo envio. As autoridades só foram notificadas em 7 de outubro.
A polícia da Filadélfia informou que seus mecanismos de segurança impediram que a mensagem avançasse para uma investigação. Também afirmou não ter encontrado indícios de invasão aos sistemas do departamento.
Polícia cobra medidas de segurança
Apesar de a denúncia ter sido retida como spam, a corporação considerou grave a apresentação de informações falsas como se fossem um relato legítimo sobre um homicídio.

La otra madre bien podría ser un remake de la icónica Coraline de Henry Selick. De hecho, ambas cintas comparten la misma idea de una familia que termina convirtiéndote en objeto de horrores. Pero mientras el clásico del stop motion logra profundizar en el tema con habilidad y volverlo impredecible, la versión de Rob Savage falla. articles.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
articles.summary:
In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft’s CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject. He calls for building a more transparent system where models can be contained, observed, and leaves behind “tamper-proof human readable evidence.”
Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
Microsoft’s CEO calls for putting an ‘emergency brake’ on AI.
Many of his recommendations align with what we’ve heard from others in the industry: timely incident disclosure, independent audits, verifiable data, and containment. It’s on that last point that he appears to go slightly farther than some others in the field, saying:
We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start. Think of it like an emergency brake. An authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task. More advanced models will require more advanced containment technologies that we need to standardize on.
Unfortunately, Nadella also refers to AI as “super intelligence” throughout the post.

AMD has reportedly raised the price of the GDDR6 memory it supplies to its board partners, with the change said to be in effect since October 1. The claim comes from a post on the Chinese forum Board Channels, and it doesn't mention a percentage or a dollar figure. AMD sells its GPUs to add-in board (AIB) partners bundled with memory, so a costlier kit usually ends up in the retail price of the finished card. The timing matches the higher suggested Radeon prices in China reported earlier this week, where the RX 9070 went up by the equivalent of $104 and the RX 9060 XT 8 GB by $45, while the RX 9070 XT was left untouched.
NVIDIA, however, apparently hasn't sent its partners a similar notice for GDDR7 this time, and the same post suggests the company may not touch memory pricing again this year. That would be a small relief for GeForce buyers, although NVIDIA already raised GDDR6 and GDDR7 kit prices in July, and the RTX 5090 was tracked at 136% above MSRP globally in early September. AMD's partners have been through this a few times in 2026 already. A 10% hike on Radeon GPU kits was reported for July, and in September there was word of another 10% increase across GPUs, chipsets, and possibly CPUs, tied to rising TSMC wafer costs. AMD hasn't confirmed the latest increase, and we don't know how much or how soon store prices outside China will move.

articles.title: Este mapa de 1922 dibuja cómo se conectaban Roma, India y China hace casi 2.000 años
articles.summary:
El concepto de "Rutas de la Seda" tal y como lo conocemos hoy en día nació en el siglo XIX y desde el principio estuvo ligada a Roma. En el discurso colonial de la época, las naciones europeas veían al Imperio romano como el primer gran ejemplo de hegemonía imperial. Y no era para menos: hubo un momento en el que sus fronteras abarcaban tres continentes: desde Gran Bretaña a los Cárpatos en Europa, pero también el norte de África y Asia menor. Y eso, sus dominios. Otra cosa diferente y mucho más extensa es hasta dónde llegaban sus redes. Spoiler: de Roma no se libraba ni China.
Este mapa data de 1922 y es obra del arqueólogo y geógrafo Albert Herrmann y se llama "Las vías de comunicación entre China, India y Roma hacia 100 d.C." articles.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has recently made Traces available in open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to the rest of the request path. Security rules, transformations, cache decisions, routing, Worker execution, and origin handling now appear as OpenTelemetry spans in a single request-level timeline, without any instrumentation to write. A pricing change arrives with it, and it applies to Workers Tracing too.
This fills a well-known gap for developers running distributed tracing through a proxy. Previously, the trace showed the client and then the application, with everything in between inferred from logs and configuration. Each supported step now arrives as a span with its timing, outcome, and attributes.
The questions Cloudflare uses as examples are the ones developers actually open tickets about. Which security rule blocked the request, and how long did rule evaluation take? Did a Transform Rule rewrite the URL before the application received it, and where did that happen relative to routing? Which Page Rule, Snippet, or Worker handled the request, and which route pattern matched? And where did the time go: one example shows a cache miss where 527ms of a 539ms request went to getting a response from the origin.
Nested cache, upstream, and origin spans showing where a request spent its time (Source: Cloudflare blog post)

articles.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Cloudflare announced Friday that it’s acquiring Deno, the startup behind the programming runtime of the same name.
According to Cloudflare’s Kenton Varda, Cloudflare will use this acquisition to improve its Workers programming model and platform, which allows customers to build and run software on Cloudflare’s network. (Varda is principal engineer for Cloudflare Workers.)
Deno — which was co-founded by Bert Belder and Node.js creator Ryan Dahl — recently launched celld, an open source implementation of Workers, which Varda wrote “delighted” the Cloudflare team. Varda argued that contrary to “a popular theory” that the company “made Cloudflare Workers work differently from other cloud platforms in order to create ‘lock-in,’” the company believes “being open source and giving people an escape hatch is good business.”
Dahl, meanwhile, wrote that his team is “joining Cloudflare to make the Workers programming model a mainstream way to build servers.”
The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. Deno had raised a total of $26 million, including a Series A led by Sequoia.

Ursächlich für diese Lücke war allerdings lediglich eine buchhalterische Anpassung: Während Konkurrenten wie Anthropic über Cloud-Partner generierte Bruttoumsätze voll verbuchen, weist OpenAI nur die tatsächlich einbehaltenen Nettoanteile aus.
Dennoch lenkt dieser Vorfall den Blick auf die generelle Rentabilität aktueller KI-Investitionen. Wie Bloomberg berichtet, äußerte sich der Analyst Joachim Klement von der Investmentbank Panmure Liberum kritisch zu den derzeitigen Entwicklungen.
Klement prognostiziert, dass die aktuelle Investitionsblase im KI-Sektor in den Jahren 2027 oder 2028 platzen wird. Er begründet dies mit einer fehlerhaften Ausrichtung der Branche. Derzeit fließen erhebliche Mittel in sogenannte Frontier-Modelle, also sehr große und rechenintensive Sprachmodelle, die in zentralen Rechenzentren betrieben werden.
Die Rolle lokaler Modelle
Die tatsächliche Entwicklung könnte laut Klement in eine andere Richtung verlaufen. As AI gobbles up an ever larger amount of energy, the hunt is on for efficient and cost-effective power sources. One of the companies leading the charge is Petra Power.
Petra, which was founded in 2017, sells solid oxide fuel cells — ceramic devices that convert fuel, like natural gas, into electric power without burning it. The company markets them as a more efficient and environmentally friendly way to operate data centers and large vehicles.
Petra’s founder, Aaron Goodman, told TechCrunch that his company’s product has significantly lower fuel costs and emissions than traditional power sources, and that they have much less of a physical footprint, too, because they’re more compact and lightweight.
The efficiency, and the cost savings that come with it, is what makes the fuel cells attractive. “Combustion takes fuel and creates explosions,” Goodman said, describing how traditional power generation works. “Those explosions create heat. That heat creates motion. The motion powers an electromotive force, which eventually creates electricity. It’s a lot of steps, and they all have so much loss in them that you end up with a really inefficient system.”
Petra’s fuel cells skip most of these steps. “What fuel cells do is they take the electrons directly off of the fuel, so they strip the fuel of its electrons, which creates electricity,” he explained. “It’s one step, no loss, and subsequently, in theory, at least, they’re much, much more efficient.”

As first reported in MacRumors, Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.”
Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.”)
In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down, with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data.
“The team is moving on to new things, and we won’t be continuing development of the product,” the company said. It also thanked its users, saying, “The fact that you used it, told friends about it, sent us your suggestions and your ideas, made it feel like we built it together.”

Besitzer einer Fritzbox können auf ein so kompliziertes Setup zukünftig allerdings verzichten. Denn ab Fritz OS 8.40 beziehungsweise 8.50 könnt ihr direkt auf den Routern des deutschen Herstellers Filterlisten hinterlegen, mit denen auch der Abruf von Werbeanzeigen durch euren Smart-TV unterbunden werden kann.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.
In a Saturday morning post on X, Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
“We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI.
As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”
“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said. “Think of it like an emergency brake.”
Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models, and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development.

Il y a des irritations numériques qu'on finit par tolérer à force d'habitude. On World Mental Health Day, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar explains how AI, screen time and meditation affect creativity, mental wellbeing and human connection.
Some years ago, our attention span was 45 to 50 minutes. Today, it has reduced to just 47 seconds. There is a severe attention deficit today.
The increased use of screens has a big role to play in this. When we stare at a screen for too long, we blink less. That affects the freshness and creativity of our minds. People today have more experiences than their senses and minds can handle. They feel emotionally exhausted and inwardly lost.
The purpose of technology is to bring us comfort. If it becomes the cause of distress, its purpose is lost. Holding onto cell phones all day hurts the nervous system. But if you are free from stress, you will use technology for a good purpose.
AI can have three interpretations.
The first is the absence of intelligence. A lot of what comes on social media is fake and AI-driven. We have to move ahead in AI, but with awareness. We forget to recognise intelligence in nature, which is an absence of intelligence on our part.
The second is artificial intelligence. It can only reproduce what is already stored, not create something new. It challenges our intellect and creativity, and pushes us to do something original. Esta es una buena noticia, de esas que apetece leer. En las Huertas de Formiga, a los pies de la sierra de Guara, nacen dos fuentes a pocos metros una de otra. Una da agua dulce. La otra, salada. Y ambos se juntan y riegan los bancales de un veterano agricultor en Panzano (Huesca), Francisco Bescós, dando lugar a hortalizas únicas en España.
O eso sostiene el profesor de cocina Ismael Ferrer, que escribió sobre este hombre de 73 años que mantenía su huerta contra viento y marea. Atribuyó a esa mezcla de aguas el sabor de sus hortalizas. El problema es que en esa tierra maduraron las calabazas de su familia durante generaciones, pero ahora Bescós deja de plantarlas. Ya no tiene edad para seguir. Así que ha tomado una medida: regalar su bien más preciado.
Qué entregó. Un plantío germinado, con sus cepellones. Dentro, dos variedades: la calabaza amarilla de Panzano y la de Rabique. De la primera, Bescós cuenta que la conoce en casa desde sus abuelos, dice que son como son desde hace 200 años. Además de agricultor, lleva años estudiando la etnografía local.
Ismael Ferrer, profesor y divulgador, será quien se haga cargo de tan valiosa herencia. Él dirige la parte gastronómica del CIGA y es autor del mapa de legumbres y hortalizas de Aragón. articles.title: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
articles.summary:
For about a decade, the mainstream understanding has been that psychedelics cause chaos in the brain. Brain networks—the stable patterns of communication that handle vision, attention, or our sense of self, and more—loosen and start talking to each other all at once. EEG traces get noisier and more complex. “Think of the networks of the brain as highways,” says Devon Stoliker, a neuroscientist at Monash University. “Under psychedelics, these highways break down into many different directions.”
In a recent Nature study, Stoliker’s team designed an experiment to test whether these directions are truly chaotic and random. Researchers gathered 62 people who had never taken a psychedelic before, gave them 19 milligrams of psilocybin, a common psychedelic found in certain fungi, and scanned their brains. Then, they used AI to analyze the drugged and sober brain scans. What emerged was not exactly chaos.
An uninterrupted trip
Stoliker thinks chaos is not a satisfactory explanation for psychedelics’ effect on the brain. “It never really explained why an individual would have a meaningful experience, why they might have insight, why they might experience clarity, and why these might translate into positive psychological changes,” Stoliker says. To investigate if there are other explanations, he and his colleagues designed a study called PsiConnect.

articles.title: Google presenta teclado para escribir con una mano: sus botones se desplazan sobre una cinta transportadora

La división japonesa de Google presentó un teclado experimental que invierte la lógica tradicional de escritura: en lugar de que el usuario mueva los dedos hacia las teclas, son las teclas las que se desplazan hacia el dedo. El dispositivo, bautizado Gboard Conveyor Belt Version, monta sus botones sobre cuatro cintas transportadoras que giran en bucle hasta que el carácter deseado llega frente al usuario.
El nombre original en japonés, Gboard kurukuru version, hace referencia a la palabra kuru, que se traduce aproximadamente como “acercarse o llegar”, y alude al movimiento circular y repetitivo de las cintas. El equipo de Gboard explicó que la idea parte de una observación simple: los teclados convencionales están diseñados para dos manos, por lo que escribir con una sola mano o un solo dedo obliga a desplazar todo el brazo y la palma por la superficie del dispositivo.
Cuatro cintas con 29 teclas cada una
El diseño distribuye 116 teclas en total, repartidas en cuatro bandas con 29 caracteres cada una. El usuario presiona el carácter en el momento exacto en que pasa frente a su dedo. A diferencia de los teclados tradicionales, las mayúsculas y minúsculas tienen botones separados, sin necesidad de recurrir a la tecla Shift, una decisión que la compañía considera más intuitiva para este formato.

Dyson is already a familiar name in personal care, thanks to its now well established hair-styling gadgets, so a move into oral care wasn't entirely left-field. When I caught up with Jake Dyson — son of founder, James, and Dyson's chief engineer — at the brand's Unveiled event, I wanted to know what prompted such a move. And, more broadly, how a brand might end up with such a twisty, turny product roadmap.
(For clarity, throughout this article I'll be using "Dyson" to mean the brand, and "Jake" to mean the person.)

Cuando pensamos en el lobo, irremediablemente lo asociamos a un depredador de ciervos, ovejas, conejos y similares, , pero su dieta es más variada de lo que parece. De hecho, algunas manadas en verano comen mucha fruta. Y resulta que ese hábito frugívoro tiene consecuencias para el medio ambiente: sin ir más lejos, son una bendición para los arándanos.
Ojalá me coma un lobo. No dijo nadie nunca, salvo quizás los arándanos: un estudio de la Universidad de Minnesota ha descubierto el efecto de los lobos (de su ingesta) sobre la germinación de los arándanos. Concretamente, aquellas semillas que se habían comido los lobos germinaron en un 96 % frente al 69% de las que no. Además, también germinaron más rápido: para el día 19 ya habían salido la mitad, mientras que para las semillas no digeridas hubo que esperar hasta el día 26.
La digestión es una bendición. Vaya por delante algo, la ingestión de semillas por animales suele aumentar la germinación y hasta la calidad, sirva como ejemplo el café de civeta que se llama así porque sale de la civeta, un pequeño mamífero similar a un hurón. Eso sí, depende del tipo de animal: entre los cánidos hay resultados desiguales: zorros rojos y coyotes la mejoran, pero otras especies como perros domésticos, zorros grises, zorros cangrejeros y también coyotes, la reducen o no la modifican.

Un hielo que, según los estudios publicados hasta ahora, debe tener un 25% de polvo. Este no es un dato trivial. La cantidad de polvo que hay en el hielo de un planeta puede decirnos muchas cosas sobre su habitabilidad. El problema es que, según un estudio publicado recientemente por científicos de la Universidad de Washington, ese dato estaba posiblemente sobreestimado. Más bien, parece que en el hielo del planeta rojo hay solo un 3% de polvo. Ahora bien, ¿qué tiene que ver eso con la presencia o ausencia de vida?
Un método inadecuado. Normalmente, los cálculos sobre la cantidad de polvo en el hielo marciano se realizaban mediante un método desarrollado a partir del regolito lunar. Se pensaba que el mismo método podría usarse para cualquier material en cualquier planeta. Sin embargo, cuando se probó para medir los niveles de polvo en el hielo de la Tierra, los datos eran incoherentes con la realidad.
Por eso, los autores de este nuevo estudio decidieron usar un método más específico, que sí resulta eficaz en el hielo terrestre. Cuando lo probaron con los datos espectrales del hielo marciano tomados por sondas como Mars Express o Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, encontraron que se había estado sobreestimando la cantidad de polvo. ¿El primer rascacielos africano? Allá por el año 800 a. C., en Yeha, en la región de Tigray en el norte del mencionado país africano se levantó un palacio llamado Grat Be'al Gibri. Hoy está en ruinas, reducido a parte de la planta baja y poco más, como puedes ver en la imagen que ilustra este artículo. articles.title: Dormir 80 minutos menos durante seis semanas nos hace engordar, según un nuevo estudio

Aun así, no dejan de sorprendernos las nuevas consecuencias que se van descubriendo que podría acarrear descansar durante menos tiempo. Por ejemplo, según un estudio reciente, dormir poco podría hacernos engordar, con todo lo que eso conlleva.
Solo seis semanas. En este estudio participaron 95 personas con riesgo cardiometabólico elevado, que aseguraron dormir normalmente más de 7 horas. Durante seis semanas, algunos tuvieron que acostarse 90 minutos más tarde. Equivaldría más o menos a 80 minutos menos de sueño. Después, durante otras seis semanas, volvieron a su rutina de sueño habitual. Otros hicieron lo mismo, pero en orden inverso: primero el sueño adecuado y después el restringido. A lo largo de las 12 semanas que duró el estudio se analizaron tanto su sueño como su actividad mediante pulseras.
Además, se tomaron datos de su peso, la circunferencia de la cintura, la composición corporal y los niveles de hormonas asociadas al apetito. Al comparar todos estos datos, se vio que esas seis semanas fueron suficientes para alterar su peso.
Medio kilo. De media, los participantes ganaron una libra de peso, equivalente más o menos a medio kilo. Esto puede parecernos poco. Sin embargo, los autores del estudio recuerdan que solo se hizo un análisis de seis semanas. Si lo extrapolamos a un año entero, la ganancia de peso puede ser considerable. articles.title: Por qué faltan diez días en el calendario de tu móvil si viajas hasta octubre de 1582
articles.summary:
Si abres el calendario de un iPhone y retrocedes más de cuatro siglos, vas a encontrarte con una curiosidad: del 4 de octubre de 1582 pasa al 15 de octubre. Esto solo te serviría si tuvieras un DeLorean y quisieras viajar a esa fecha concreta, aunque detrás de esos diez días que se evaporan sin dejar rastro hay una explicación. Apple es consciente de esa laguna temporal.
Once minutos y catorce segundos. Julio César instauró el calendario juliano en el año 45 a. C. Para ese calendario el año duraba 365,25 días. Y tenía un bisiesto cada cuatro años. Astronómicamente hablando, el año solar ronda los 365,2422 días. Esa diferencia de 11 minutos y 14 segundos al año generaba un día entero de desfase cada 130 años aproximadamente.
En el siglo XVI, el retraso acumulado por el calendario juliano era de diez días. No habría habido problemas de no ser por la religión: el Concilio de Nicea del año 325 fijó la Pascua tras el equinoccio de primavera del 21 de marzo. Para 1582, el equinoccio real se iba al 11 de marzo. De seguir acumulando desfase en el calendario, la Pascua corría el riesgo de terminar en verano.
Dormir el cuatro y despertar el quince. El papa Gregorio XIII promulgó en febrero de 1582 la bula Inter gravissimas. Para corregir unos doce siglos y medio de desviación astronómica, la Iglesia tomó una decisión: aparte de adoptar el nuevo calendario gregoriano, borró de este diez días. Desaparecieron.

articles.title: En 1971, Québec inundó 11.500 km² de bosque para crear un megaembalse y, sin saberlo, envenenó a un pueblo entero

Sin embargo, al crear embalses enormes en medio de la naturaleza salvaje, se desencadenó una bomba química silenciosa a consecuencia de la liberación del mercurio natural del suelo que envenenó el pescado del que dependía históricamente el pueblo indígena de los Cree.
Un gran problema. Un pescado que se saque de estas aguas a simple vista puede estar en perfecto estado y, sin embargo, ser un grave riesgo para el sistema nervioso de aquellas personas que decidan comerlo. Esta es la dura realidad con la que se topó el pueblo Cree tras la construcción de este gran complejo hidroeléctrico que alteró cinco ríos y la creación de inmensos embalses sumergieron más de 11.500 km2 de bosque boreal, un área comparable con la superficie de Qatar.
Pero la contaminación no fueron los generadores eléctricos ni la maquinaria pesada, sino el contacto de la propia agua con la tierra virgen.
El mercurio es una de esas toxinas de las que nos preocupamos mucho, sobre todo cuando vamos a tomar pescado. Pero en este caso el mercurio no provino de la contaminación industrial, sino que llevaba miles de años depositado en el suelo forestal. We've seen AI inventing fake facts and spewing out hiking plans that put people in danger, but the technology has now progressed to the level of sending false, unsolicited tip-offs to the police about unsolved murder cases.
An Anthropic AI model emailed the Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tip line on July 18, TechCrunch reports, having come across the PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com portal during a website interaction test and learning about the case.
As the email went to the PPD spam folder it wasn't followed up on, and it appears no one was aware of the incident until Anthropic found out what had happened on September 28. The company then contacted the cops on Wednesday, October 7.

But businesses should not be locked into a single machine
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is great at generating valuable insights, but what companies end up doing with those insights - that’s where true achievement lies, and that’s what companies should be focusing on.
This is one of the core messages delivered by Ryan Waite, Director of Open Source Ecosystems and Incubations at Microsoft, during his keynote, “From Open Source to Agentic Systems: Building the AI Native Era” at the Open Source Summit.
Waite described the interaction between AI and human expertise as a learning loop, a kind of hill-climbing machine that helps businesses improve, and keep on improving.
The knowledge belongs to the business
AI models are great at processing enormous amounts of information and generating insights at a scale humans cannot match (and sometimes cannot even fathom), but people bring something arguably more important to the table: context and judgement.
Putting insights into wider context, and using that to make conclusions, helps employees turn information into knowledge, and that knowledge later becomes part of the organization’s collective expertise. And with every iteration the knowledge grows, helping businesses climb further up the proverbial mountain.

articles.title: Nikon le quitó el primer premio a un video científico por usar inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
La empresa japonesa Nikon retiró el primer premio de su concurso de fotografía microscópica Small World in Motion después de confirmar que el video ganador había sido manipulado con inteligencia artificial, algo que las reglas del certamen prohíben expresamente.
El video, presentado por el investigador Ning Xu, mostraba lo que describía como estructuras parecidas a pelos que recubren las vías respiratorias moviéndose de forma irregular en un niño con discinesia ciliar primaria, una enfermedad respiratoria poco frecuente.
Nikon anunció la decisión el 9 de octubre a través de un comunicado publicado en su sitio oficial. “Tras reevaluar minuciosamente el video y el material adjunto, y consultar con miembros del jurado, determinamos que el video ganador no cumplía con las reglas del certamen sobre inteligencia artificial generativa”, informó la compañía.
El reglamento del concurso, vigente desde hace quince años, es explícito: “No se permiten videos generados por inteligencia artificial, y el organizador tiene derecho a solicitar el material original para su verificación”.
Las sospechas que empezaron en redes
El premio se había entregado un mes antes, pero científicos y ex jurados del certamen denunciaron en la red social LinkedIn que las estructuras celulares del video aparecían y desaparecían de un modo imposible en la biología real, según reportó la cadena BBC.

articles.title: Does a VPN protect your privacy when using ChatGPT or Claude?

Does a VPN protect your privacy when using ChatGPT or Claude? What network encryption can and can’t hide from AI
A VPN is great at hiding where you are and what your internet provider sees. However, when you’re chatting with ChatGPT or Claude, your privacy depends on something far more complicated than a tunnel through the internet.
Even the best VPNs won’t stop AI companies from reading, storing, and learning from everything you type. In this article, we’ll unpack exactly what data these platforms see, why encryption has limits, and what you can actually do to protect yourself.
What chatbots see (and what a VPN actually hides)
Without a VPN, OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude) can typically see a lot about your connection. Your IP address reveals your approximate geographic location. Device metadata follows alongside that, including your browser type, operating system, and unique device identifiers.
According to OpenAI’s privacy policy, the company collects your IP address; device information, including unique identifiers; cookie data; and your location, along with your email address and payment information.
Anthropic does the same. Their policy covers location, connection details, and device usage patterns, especially on the mobile app. Different wording, same result: both companies can see roughly where you are and what you’re using to talk to them.

Los vehículos eléctricos a batería, conocidos como BEV, utilizan uno o varios motores eléctricos alimentados por una batería.

Este procedimiento permite restaurar conversaciones almacenadas previamente, aunque tiene una condición importante: la información recibida o enviada después de la última copia podría perderse al recuperar una versión anterior del historial.

Los pasos generales son los mismos en celulares Android y iPhone: comprobar la copia de seguridad, reinstalar WhatsApp y restaurar el historial durante la configuración. Sin embargo, el almacenamiento en la nube cambia según el sistema operativo: Android utiliza Google Drive y iPhone emplea iCloud.

articles.title: The Third-Party Agent Problem: Why Security Built for AI You Chose Misses the Agents You Didn't
articles.summary:
In environments studied for the 2026 State of Agent Security Report, roughly 1,280 third-party products now embed AI. About 282 of them sit behind single sign-on. The other thousand are invisible to identity infrastructure by default, not because anyone hid them, but because an identity stack can only govern what authenticates through it, and most agents never do.
That gap is the clearest expression of a shift the security industry is only starting to name. For several years, "AI security" solved a first-party problem: the company decided to use AI, procured licenses, deployed a model behind a gateway, and security pointed controls at the thing the business had chosen. Agents do not arrive that way. They arrive inside software the enterprise already runs, and they arrive without a decision.
Why the decision point mattered more than the controls
Every control in the first-party toolkit assumes a moment exists: model scanning assumes a model was selected, prompt inspection assumes a gateway was deployed, an acceptable-use policy assumes there was an adoption to accept. That moment gave security a review, a surface to instrument, and an owner to name.
Agents skip the moment. Salesforce's Slack Code, launched in August 2026, lets a user tag a coding agent into any conversation; the agent reads the shared context, writes the code, and opens the pull request. articles.title: Intel y AMD resucitan la memoria DDR4 para esquivar la crisis de precios de la RAM
articles.summary:
Intel y AMD volvieron a habilitar el soporte para la memoria DDR4, un estándar de más de una década de antigüedad, como respuesta directa a la escalada de precios que atraviesa la industria de la memoria RAM en todo el mundo.
La fabricante taiwanesa de placas madre Gigabyte anunció que dos de sus líneas admitirán los próximos procesadores construidos sobre el zócalo LGA 1700 de Intel, el conector físico que une el chip a la placa.
Ese zócalo había debutado en 2021 junto a los procesadores Alder Lake de duodécima generación y fue, en su momento, el único capaz de admitir tanto memoria DDR4 como la más moderna DDR5 al mismo tiempo.
Intel lo había discontinuado en 2024 para pasar a una estrategia exclusiva de DDR5. Según Gigabyte, los nuevos chips compatibles con LGA 1700 se esperan para comienzos de 2027.
La memoria DDR4 es un tipo de memoria RAM para computadoras. Usa menos energía que la DDR3, ya que funciona con 1,2 voltios, y puede alcanzar velocidades de entre 2133 y 3200 MHz o más en modelos especiales.
Las nuevas placas y procesadores compatibles con DDR4 llegarán recién en los primeros meses de 2027.
Por qué regresó la memoria DDR4
La decisión responde a una brecha de precios que se volvió insostenible para buena parte de los usuarios que quieren actualizar su computadora.
Según The Verge, un kit de 32 gigabytes de memoria DDR5 de la marca Corsair cuesta actualmente USD 620, mientras que el kit equivalente de DDR4 se consigue por USD 260, menos de la mitad.

AWS is building a massive 36-building, 1,100-acre data center campus in Pennsylvania — Homer City Energy Campus will create around 1,500-2,000 jobs and be powered by natural gas
A new 4.5GW gas plant will supply most of the electricity for AWS
- AWS plans 36 data centers across 1,100 acres in Pennsylvania
- Homer City is replacing a 2GW coal station with gas-powered computing infrastructure
- The AWS campus will stretch across six sites in Indiana County
Amazon Web Services (AWS) has filed plans for a 36-building data center development spanning 1,100 acres in Indiana County, Pennsylvania.
The Homer City Energy Campus will rely mainly on a new 4.5GW natural gas generation facility being developed alongside the project.
AWS expects the development to create between 1,500 and 2,000 jobs, with average annual salaries ranging from $80,000 to $100,000.
A huge campus backed by natural gas
The planned complex will sit across six areas in Center and Blacklick townships, roughly 50 miles east of Pittsburgh.
Each of the 36 data center buildings will contain two floors, reach 70 feet, and provide approximately 225,000 square feet.
AWS also plans offices, storage facilities, electrical substations, security infrastructure, and additional generation equipment supporting the large computing operation.
Construction is scheduled across four stages, beginning in December 2026, with the final stage scheduled to start during January 2032.

articles.title: Megan Fox se une a plataforma de contenido explícito: qué otros artistas exploran esta tecnología
articles.summary:
El modelo de negocio del entretenimiento ha experimentado una de las transformaciones más drásticas de la última década. Lo que antes se gestionaba a través de contratos de exclusividad con grandes estudios y agencias de representación, hoy se controla directamente desde la pantalla de un teléfono inteligente.
La reciente incursión de Megan Fox como copropietaria y partícipe de la plataforma Subs.com es el ejemplo más reciente de un fenómeno que lleva años gestándose: la migración masiva de celebridades hacia el mercado de las suscripciones directas de contenido.
Este es el recorrido cronológico de las celebridades que han incursionado en este modelo de negocio:
Agosto de 2020: Bella Thorne
El verdadero punto de inflexión en la industria ocurrió con la actriz y ex-estrella de Disney. Su debut fue tan masivo que colapsó los servidores de OnlyFans y logró recaudar un millón de dólares en sus primeras 24 horas. Aunque su llegada generó controversia dentro de la comunidad de creadores tradicionales por las expectativas de los usuarios, Thorne demostró el poder de la monetización masiva e inmediata sin intermediarios en Hollywood.

articles.title: Grandes editoriales de Estados Unidos usan IA en secreto y sus empleados se rebelan
articles.summary:
Empleados de tres de las cinco editoriales más grandes de Estados Unidos, HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster y Hachette, usan herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa para escribir correos a agentes literarios, textos de contratapa y materiales de marketing sin avisar a los autores, según una investigación de la revista Wired.
El reportaje, basado en entrevistas con más de dos docenas de trabajadores que pidieron mantener el anonimato para proteger sus empleos, describe un uso extendido de modelos como Claude y ChatGPT para generar texto a partir de instrucciones escritas. Según los testimonios, también se emplean para diseñar portadas y producir videos publicitarios.
El contraste llama la atención porque, durante el último año, las mismas editoriales demandaron a empresas de inteligencia artificial por infracción de derechos de autor y cancelaron contratos de libros sospechados de haber sido escritos con asistencia de modelos de lenguaje, como la novela de terror Shy Girl de Hachette o el thriller Call Me, I’ll Hide the Body de Macmillan.
Lo que nadie anunció puertas adentro
En HarperCollins, los directivos compraron licencias de Claude a Anthropic y más tarde sumaron ChatGPT y Jasper, una plataforma que promete ejecutar campañas de marketing de punta a punta. Decenas de empleados fueron designados, sin pedirles opinión, como “campeones de IA” encargados de encontrar nuevos usos en sesiones mensuales de lluvia de ideas.
